title: How brewers can protect beers from smoke-tainted hops
author: Jennifer Ouellette
body: The 2020 Oregon wildfires burned over 1 million acres, destroyed thousands of structures, and killed 11 people. Smoke from the fires spread across the entire region; this "smoke taint" adversely affected not only local wine production , but also hops grown for beer brewing. Since the Pacific Northwest produces more than 95 percent of US hops and about 40 percent of the global supply, the potential economic impact is significant. That's why Oregon State University (OSU) scientists have been studying how brewers could offset the negative impacts of smoke taint while still incorporating affected hops in their brews. Most recently, they found that it all depends on how much tainted hops are included and when hops are added during the brewing process, according to a new paper published in the Journal of the American Society of Brewing Chemists. As previously reported , the chemistry of brewing beer is a very active area of research. For instance, i n 2018 , OSU chemist Thomas Shellhammer—who also co-authored this latest paper— identified the growing popularity of " dry hopping " (adding hops after fermentation, common for pale ales) among craft brewers as the likely culprit of the exploding beer bottle phenomenon. title: Google filed a patent application for an AI TV channel starring you
body: Ever since Google introduced its Veo 3 AI video model in March 2025, AI-generated video has started appearing in social feeds, ads, and even movies on free streaming services . Now, Google has sketched out how AI could make the person watching TV the star of their own show. In a patent application published Nov. 19, the company describes a feature called "My Channel," which would use a viewer's watch history to generate videos for them. In one version, the system could use the viewer's likeness and voice to cast them as the lead of their very own TV show. Patsnap, the database that hosts the filing, offers an AI-generated "technical title" that sums up the idea as a way of "enhancing user engagement." The patent-tracking site Patentlyze first spotted the filing and shared it with 404 Media, which covered it on Nov. 23. Patent records show that Google filed the application on May 13, 2025, but the company has yet to announce a product. What would be on My Channel? One drawing in the application shows a TV menu called "John's Channel," with a crime comedy, a rom-com, a sci-fi adventure, and an action thriller. In a sample prompt, the filing tells the AI to make a video where "the user will play the protagonist." Another example takes that a step further. If a cricket fan has been watching clips about a particular player, the AI could put them in a scene with that player or show them "cheering for India in the stands." title: Tidal announces ban on AI-generated music; 27 million tracks will be deleted
author: Ryan Whitwam
body: Most streaming music providers have opted to label AI-generated content on their platforms, and until now, Tidal was one of them. However, the company is about to take a harder stance. Tidal announced that in the coming weeks, it will fully ban AI music because of the harm it does to human artists. Tidal debuted its initial AI policy in July 2026, which included labeling and demonetizing all songs created entirely with AI. That wasn't enough to stem the tide of AI slop, though. Over the past 90 days, Tidal reports that 43 percent of new uploads were completely AI-generated. On November 6, new uploads to Tidal hit a whopping 60 percent AI-generated. As things stand, Tidal hosts 27 million tracks labeled as AI, all of which were obviously added in the past couple of years. That accounts for 6.3 percent of Tidal's total catalog. On December 9, Tidal will delete all those songs. The streamer notes this will have essentially no negative impact because 96 percent of AI-labeled tracks got zero plays in the past 90 days. Throughout its announcement, Tidal is careful to stipulate that it's only talking about music that has been fully created by AI. Artists can still use AI tools as long as the final product contains human elements. Read full article Comments

title: Porsche 718 Boxster prototype drive: This electric roadster is real
author: Tim Stevens
body: Porsche provided flights from Albany, New York, to Los Angeles and accommodation so Ars could drive the 718 EV prototype. Ars does not accept paid editorial content. It wasn't until I was stuck in traffic on the way back from a run up and down some canyon roads that I realized just how low Porsche's upcoming all-electric 718 Boxster truly is. I was idly looking around at the other cars, doing the math on the EV adoption rate in this small sample of Los Angeles gridlock (roughly 50 percent, impressively) when I noticed that I was eye-level with a Tesla Model Y door handle. That's not particularly low for a sports car, but it's practically unheard of for an EV. Nearly all modern electric cars are built atop a skateboard-style battery pack, a stack of cells that elevates the seating position by a good 3 inches. In these SUV-heady days, that's usually not a problem, possibly even an advantage. But, in a car like this, the closer you can get your keister to the road, the greater the sensation of speed. So, for the company's first all-electric sports car, the 718 Boxster that will be fully revealed next year, Porsche engineers put the battery pack behind the driver. That powers a single motor spinning the rear wheels and creates a driving experience that both honors the simple joy of motoring in a mid-engined Boxster while pushing the 718 to new heights of power and performance. The list of so-called "funding anomalies" is dominated largely by appropriations for the Department of Defense, including the Golden Dome missile defense program championed by the Trump administration. The funding represents a significant 25 percent boost for NASA's Artemis program, which received approximately $7.8 billion in fiscal year 2026. Technically, the White House is seeking to increase the annualized funding rate for Artemis to $9.8 billion, rather than immediately providing NASA with an additional $2 billion. title: Homo erectus lived in the rainforest alongside Denisovans
author: Kiona N. Smith
body: Homo erectus was walking around mainland Asia at least 60,000 years more recently than archaeologists thought. A handful of teeth from two caves in southern China's Guangxi Province just filled in a significant gap in the fossil record of a region that's vital to the story of how our genus, Homo , took over the world. The chemical makeup of the teeth's enamel suggests that, over the course of their lives, these Homo erectus moved across surprisingly large distances and made their living in dense tropical rainforests—an environment we'd previously assumed that only our species had ever gained a real foothold in. And one of the teeth offers a strong clue that Homo erectus probably shared this vast landscape with the Denisovans. A handful of teeth with a lot to say Baxian and Naxian are a pair of limestone caves that lie 15 kilometers apart along a karst valley corridor in southern China. University of Copenhagen paleoanthropologist Frido Welker and his colleagues unearthed a total of nine hominin teeth from among the more than 18,000 bones and fragments from non-hominin animals found there. Macquarie University paleoanthropologist Kira Westaway and her colleagues analyzed proteins and chemical isotopes from the enamel of five of these teeth. Read full article Comments

title: Amazon says hackers' AI agents found and exploited 0-day with little human input
author: Dan Goodin
body: Amazon said AI agents recently found and exploited a zero-day vulnerability with no human oversight beyond a simple instruction to get root access on an East Asian university server. The agents were running on Cairn, an open source AI penetration-testing framework. The hackers, who provided prompts in simplified Chinese and configured the model to the Chinese Standard Time zone, gave the agents a list of IP addresses and the goal: “obtain shell access.” In short order, the agents discovered a zero-day in an open source medical imaging AI application running on one of the target servers. The agents then exploited the vulnerability and gained full control of the system. “These findings show that agentic offensive operations are already happening, and defenders should prepare for the speed and persistence these tools enable,” Amazon said . title: Ukraine sinks Russian warship, strikes cargo ships from Mediterranean to Baltic
author: Jeremy Hsu
body: Ukrainian explosive naval drones sank a Russian warship docked in the port city of Benghazi in Libya while also striking a Russian cargo ship that it was escorting. The incident demonstrates the expanding scope of Ukrainian military strikes on Russian ships from the coast of North Africa to the Gulf of Finland. The Russian Navy’s missile corvette Merkury sank at port after being struck by at least two Ukrainian naval drones on November 22, according to The Associated Press . Ukraine’s Security Service described using seven naval drones launched from a mother ship to target the Merkury , and Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy shared video footage showing the drone boats approaching and exploding against both the burning Russian warship and a Russian dry cargo ship, MV Angara . Reactions to Huang's return have been a mix of praise, criticism, and jokes, with several other tech executives rallying around him. SEE ALSO: Nvidia's board reinstates Jensen Huang as CEO following Trump's endorsement Nvidia announced Huang's resignation on Nov. 12 , a day after the board accepted it with immediate effect. He stepped down amid reports that he'd had extramarital affairs with both an alleged Chinese spy and a Nvidia employee , with allegations of a third affair with another worker subsequently surfacing. His relationship with Alice Huang (no relation) drew particular scrutiny, as she was suspected of smuggling Nvidia chips. She previously led Megaspeed, a company U.S. authorities have been investigating over concerns it smuggled advanced Nvidia chips to China in circumvention of U.S. restrictions . While Huang said that he would be "honored" to return as CEO if asked, the board stated said on Nov. 17 that it did not plan to bring him back . Yet after reported pressure from President Donald Trump , the chipmaker has put Huang back in the top job after all. In a press release announcing Huang's reinstatement, Nvidia stated that it had based the decision on "input from senior levels of the United States government." The Google Threat Intelligence Group recently released a report revealing that cyberattackers are now using multi-agent AI frameworks capable of searching for vulnerabilities and exploiting them independently. Furthermore, these tactics are already being used in cyberattack campaigns. Google cybersecurity researchers uncovered "an exposed staging server hosting a multi-agent vulnerability research and weaponization framework dubbed exploit_agent," which "integrates with multiple frontier and local LLMs." Google's investigation revealed that the entity behind the server hosting this framework appeared to be specifically targeting French websites in the media and entertainment sector. Some education sites were targeted as well. Google's report cites even more examples of fully autonomous cyberattacks. In one example, the cybersecurity firm Greynoise found that a bad actor used LLMs to identify vulnerabilities and automatically build exploits. The hacker was able to put together a list of targets and then execute the exploits against hundreds of organizations. title: U.S. intelligence chief says more tech outages are inevitably coming
body: Over the past month, tech outages have disrupted work emails, delayed bank transactions, and temporarily grounded departing flights across the United States. Most of the biggest disruptions happened within six days of one another. On Sunday, Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton said Americans should expect more disruptions like these, but not because of an incoming cyberattack ; rather, because companies and government agencies are now in the process of updating aging technology. "We are going to have glitches, gaps, interruptions in service," Clayton told CNN's State of the Union on Sunday, Nov. 24. "That is going to happen." He said much of the country's digital infrastructure was built over three decades or more and needs upgrades to run better and stay secure. (As one example, the FAA is still in the process of phasing out floppy disks , with a target of retiring the '90s-era technology by 2028.) Clayton compared it to weekend maintenance at work: A company might take a system offline on Saturday and plan to have it back by 2 A.M. Sunday. If the team finds another problem during the upgrade, it might be Sunday afternoon before the system is back up. "We are taking more systems down and putting them back up than ever before," he said. SEE ALSO: Are the recent outages connected? What we know. It was a lot to keep track of in six days: On Nov. 12, some Microsoft Outlook users couldn't open their inboxes or send email. body: President Trump took to social media Monday afternoon to announce that he has ordered the US military to halt plans to detonate 68 deteriorating barrels of lead azide at an Army ammunition plant in Middletown, Iowa. Trump claimed that the fate of the unstable, highly explosive material is now in the hands of a federal court and Rob Sand, Iowa's governor-elect, who won't be sworn into office until January. The Army had planned to detonate the barrels on November 20, but delayed the blast on Thursday amid public outcry and a legal challenge from environmental groups. The explosion will launch a plume of toxic gases and neurotoxic lead that could reach up to 100 miles away from the Iowa facility, the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant (IAAAP). Iowa residents and officials said they learned of the detonation only days beforehand. The environmental groups, led by Earthjustice, claimed in an emergency court filing that the Army had not fully considered safer options for disposing of the lead azide before planning the detonation. title: States sue SpaceX to stop Grok from generating child sex images, revenge porn
author: Ashley Belanger
body: On Monday, Virginia and Oregon became the first states to sue SpaceX, alleging that Grok continues to sexualize, unchecked, real photos of mostly women and children. SpaceX acquired xAI in February and now must handle the ongoing reckoning over the controversial rollout of Grok’s “spicy mode”—a model feature Musk hyped but was soon found to generate a flood of non-consensual intimate imagery (NCII) and child sex abuse images (CSAM). Initial safeguards were so lax that Grok sometimes generated nude images without being asked . title: Surveillance pricing uses our personal data to make us pay more

body: “It costs what it costs” is a mindset I’ve found useful when encountering a sizable, but highly necessary or desired, expense. The sentiment encourages me to accept the price because that’s the accepted value of the gadget, app, or service that I really need or want. But with surveillance pricing, that comfort is no longer a given. I could end up paying more for my TV because of where I am or more for a software subscription because of my age. Surveillance pricing leverages data collected from our web history , smart devices , and apps with the goal of getting us to pay more. title: Reports: Russia may launch nuclear weapon into orbit as soon as next month
author: Stephen Clark
body: Western intelligence officials worry that Russia could launch a nuclear-armed satellite into orbit before the end of the year, suggesting the country's development of a satellite-killing weapon of mass destruction is more advanced than previously thought, German media reported Monday. The orbiting nuclear weapon would threaten thousands of satellites in low-Earth orbit, including military and commercial communications networks like Starshield and Starlink. A nuclear-armed satellite would also put at risk Western military surveillance satellites and human spaceflight platforms like the International Space Station. A nuclear detonation in orbit would be indiscriminate, also knocking out Russia's own spacecraft and Chinese satellites. US lawmakers briefed on government intelligence first disclosed Russia's ambition to deploy a space-based nuclear weapon in early 2024 . At the time, US officials said Russia had launched a test satellite in 2022 to test the effects of radiation on space hardware and pave the way for a future nuclear-armed craft, but that Russia had not yet sent a nuclear weapon into orbit. title: Michelle Branchs Are You Happy Now? is having a TikTok renaissance thanks to Netflixs The Body
body: Michelle Branch has a question for Gen Z: Are you happy now? More than two decades after its release, the singer-songwriter's 2003 breakup anthem "Are You Happy Now?" is finding a new audience on TikTok , thanks to a particularly memorable needle drop in Netflix's buzzy teen horror drama The Body . And for millennials who grew up screaming along to the song in their bedrooms, the sudden resurgence feels like a long-overdue moment of recognition and another painful reminder that we're all old AF. Welcome to the Michelle Branch renaissance. We've been expecting you. The song appears in the third episode of The Body , a psychological horror series set at a Catholic girls' school in 2004, where a dance team initiation spirals into a supernatural panic. The show's early-aughts setting provides plenty of opportunities for nostalgic needle drops, with a soundtrack featuring Kelly Clarkson, Ciara, Kylie Minogue, and No Doubt. But Branch's angsty pop-rock hit gets one of the show's most memorable musical moments. During a church service, Elise puts on a convincing display of demonic possession , collapsing as the song builds toward its explosive chorus. The juxtaposition of religious imagery, teenage hysteria, and Branch's soaring vocals makes for a scene practically engineered to go viral. Nothing says teen rebellion like faking a possession to Michelle Branch's "Are You Happy Now?" Credit: Courtesy of Netflix 2026 And that's exactly what's happening on social media. body: Updated on Monday, Nov. 23 at 12:45 p.m. ET This story has been updated with additional information on how Wall Street is responding to Jensen Huang's return and additional details on why the board reversed course . The Nvidia board of directors has voted unanimously to reinstate the embattled Jensen Huang as the company's CEO, the board announced in a surprise statement Monday morning. The move follows President Donald Trump publicly calling for Huang's return as CEO. Huang famously resigned on Nov. 12 following reports from the New York Times and the Financial Times that he had an affair with a suspected Chinese spy. In the days that followed, revelations of two more alleged extramarital affairs with Nvidia employees, no less emerged, seemingly sealing the CEO's fate. On Nov. 12, Huang announced he was resigning his position as CEO, a role he'd held since he co-founded the company in 1993. Under his leadership, Nvidia became one of the most valuable companies in the world, and in recent years, Nvidia chips have powered the fast-growing AI industry. In reinstating Huang, the board cited "input from senior levels of the United States government...that Mr. Huang s reinstatement poses no national security risk." President Trump called the board's surprise decision "correct and proper" in a post on his Truth Social website . title: RIIZE brought their online fandom into the real world. I was there to see it.
body: We need to bring back MTV Unplugged . That was one of my first thoughts on Friday night as I watched K-pop group RIIZE perform for roughly 600 fans at Brooklyn Steel in New York City. There were no elaborate stage productions or arena-sized crowds. Instead, there were stripped-down performances, candid conversations, a few wonderfully awkward moments, and a sea of smartphones held high above the audience. Seriously, everyone had their phones out. For one night in Brooklyn, RIIZE's digital fandom became a sea of smartphones. Credit: Getty Images for Spotify It's a funny contradiction, considering the entire premise of the evening was to bring digital fandom into the physical world. But maybe that's just what being a fan looks like in 2026. Even when we're standing a few feet away from our favorite artists, we still want to capture the moment, preserve it, and inevitably share it with everyone who couldn't be there. The occasion was Spotify CLOSER, a new live music series that brings artists and their most dedicated listeners together for intimate performances and conversations. After launching in Seoul in Oct., the series made its U.S. debut on Nov. 20 with RIIZE, bringing together more than 600 fans from the New York tri-state area, many of whom were identified as the group's top local listeners and selected based on their listening habits. body: Apple's most affordable and most vibrant laptop has only been out since this past March, but it sounds like the company will offer a spiffy new upgrade sooner rather than later. That's hardly a surprise, given the success of the product so far. That's what Mark Gurman of Bloomberg is reporting , anyway. In his l atest Power On newsletter , Gurman predicted that Apple will sell a second iteration of the MacBook Neo most likely by the end of March 2027. That timing is meant to line up with the iOS/macOS 27.4 upgrade cycle, at which point Gurman says we could also see the iPhone 18 and 18e models, a new OLED iPad Air, and a new budget iPad. Apple upgrading a laptop just a year after release is not unheard of. In recent years, the company has been releasing annual upgrades of its MacBook Air and Pro lines, outfitting the devices with the latest Apple Silicon, sometimes with few other changes. SEE ALSO: Apple s MacBook Neo is $50 off at Amazon its best deal ever As for what to expect from the new MacBook Neo, it doesn't sound like a hugely substantial upgrade at this point in time. From a usability standpoint, the most important thing Gurman mentioned is that the A18 Pro chip powering the original Neo will be upgraded to an A19 chip, with RAM bumped from 8GB to 12GB as well. It remains to be seen if the current $699 starting price for the MacBook Neo will go up, but it's definitely a possibility. title: Nvidia reinstates Jensen Huang: What changed and when
body: Nvidia co-founder and CEO Jensen Huang resigned from the company earlier this month. Just last week, Nvidia's board made it clear that it was not open to bringing back Jensen Huang to run the company. Today, Nov. 23, Jensen Huang has been reinstated as CEO of Nvidia. After reports of multiple affairs, including one that U.S. intelligence alleges involved a Chinese spy who successfully convinced Jensen Huang to lobby the U.S. government to change its export rules regarding China, Huang was seemingly gone from Nvidia for good. A return seemed highly unlikely, as Nvidia now faces multiple investigations into potential chip smuggling and accounting issues stemming from Huang's leadership. Now that he's back, something clearly changed. So, what just happened? President Donald Trump reportedly pressured the Nvidia board on behalf of moneyed investors, including many of the tech elite, to bring Huang back to run the company. Nvidia is widely seen as central to the U.S. economy's current AI boom. Its products power compute for some of the largest AI companies and labs, such as OpenAI and Anthropic. Tech leaders, concerned about the industry's future without Huang at the helm of Nvidia, have openly advocated for his return for weeks. Since Huang's resignation, Nvidia stock has been in a free fall. As of the market's close on Friday, Nov. 20, Nvidia stock was down nearly 28 percent from the day Huang resigned. title: Jensen Huang reinstated as Nvidia CEO, board chair
author: Kyle Orland
body: Nvidia's board of directors has voted to reinstate Jensen Huang as CEO and chairman of the board, just 11 days after he resigned in the wake of multiple scandals . The reinstatement, announced Monday morning , is "effective immediately" and was based in part on "input from senior levels of the United States government" that assured the board members that "Mr. Huang’s reinstatement poses no national security risk." That assurance comes despite Huang's admitted affair with a woman who, US intelligence sources believe, was working as a Chinese spy and allegations that Nvidia had subverted export controls meant to keep Nvidia chips from reaching China. It also comes despite multiple developing investigations from multiple different government departments into those and other alleged national security, accounting, and corporate governance failures. title: F1 in Las Vegas: You've never seen an F1 race like this before
author: Jonathan M. Gitlin
body: Las Vegas welcomed Formula 1 to its streets this past weekend. And for the first time since the event’s inception in 2023 , the Grand Prix delivered on a long-promised spectacle. The racing was closer to an IndyCar oval race than anything F1 fans will have seen since slipstreaming was the order of the day at places like Monza and Hockenheim, back when humans were still landing on the Moon and downforce had yet to fundamentally change racing. The Vegas street circuit—the one that looks like an upside-down pig—is an extreme outlier on the calendar. It has plenty of long straights, so this year’s cars still suffer from energy starvation throughout the lap, as the inadequate size of their lithium-ion hybrid batteries means they become depleted very quickly , leaving the cars on just over half power with their V6 engines operating without the benefit of the hybrid’s electric motor. But the 17 turns are mostly all low speed, so there’s no risk of seeing the cars driving demoralizingly slowly through corners that are supposed to test one’s mettle . Read full article Comments

title: GTA 6 Online release update: What we know about when it comes out.
body: Grand Theft Auto VI was released on consoles last week, with millions of players exploring Leonida on Xbox and PS5 consoles. But one major question remains: What's happening with the online mode? The GTA Online component of Grand Theft Auto V has kept that 13-year-old game relevant across three console generations, with a recent leak suggesting Rockstar makes as much as $500 million annually from microtransactions alone. One would think that means GTA VI will have a similar online offering available at launch, but that isn't the case. Per a Rockstar statement given to IGN , as well as all available marketing language on digital storefronts, GTA VI is a "single-player experience." There was no online component at launch, nor has Rockstar announced any intention of adding one after launch. Sadly, that is all the concrete information anyone can provide right now. SEE ALSO: 'GTA VI' preorders are live for PS5 and Xbox, starting at $80 with a $100 Ultimate Edition However, that doesn't mean all hope is lost. It's worth remembering that both GTA V and Red Dead Redemption 2 launched as solo experiences and got online modes later, though it was only a matter of months in both cases. Given that Rockstar hasn't even said if there will be a new GTA Online experience for VI , it's probably safe to assume the wait will be longer this time. The fact that the existing GTA Online is so wildly successful (with no signs of slowing down) means Rockstar isn't necessarily incentivized to make a new one right away. title: Moon phase today: What the Moon will look like on November 23, 2026
body: Tomorrow marks the Full Moon, but tonight's Moon already looks almost full. It's still technically in its Waxing Gibbous phase, with just a small portion of its surface left in the darkness. What is today's Moon phase? As of Monday, Nov. 23, the NASA's Daily Moon Guide tracker tells us the Moon is in the Waxing Gibbous phase, with 97% of its surface visible. If you don't have any visual aids, you can still see the Mares Tranquillitatis and Fecunditatis, as well as the Aristarchus Plateau. With binoculars, you'll also see the Grimaldi Basin, the Endymion Crater, and the Mare Nectaris. And if you have a telescope, you'll get to see all this plus the Apollo 11, 15, and 16 landing spots. When is the next Full Moon? The next Full Moon will take place on November 24. What are Moon phases? According to NASA , the Moon goes through a complete cycle of phases roughly every 29.5 days. As it orbits Earth, the portion of its sunlit surface visible to us changes, giving rise to the different lunar phases. The cycle begins with a New Moon, progresses to a Full Moon, and then gradually returns to a New Moon before starting all over again. The eight phases are: New Moon - The Moon is between Earth and the sun, so the side we see is dark (in other words, it's invisible to the eye). Waxing Crescent - A small sliver of light appears on the right side (Northern Hemisphere). First Quarter - Half of the Moon is lit on the right side. It looks like a half-Moon. title: An unseen planet past Neptune may be in Earths weight class
body: Math points to our solar system having another planet in Earth's weight class far beyond Neptune , tugging distant icy bodies onto strange orbits, a new study proposes. That would make it far smaller than Planet Nine , a hypothesized giant world five to 10 times Earth's mass that has drawn most of the attention in the hunt for an undiscovered planet. No one has spotted this suspected world, nicknamed Planet X2, but these researchers argue it would explain the strangest orbits in the outer solar system better. "Imagine discovering, after decades of mapping our solar system, that another planet has been hiding from us all this time," said lead researcher Patryk Sofia Lykawka, of Kindai University in Japan, in a statement. Every search for a missing planet has started the same way, with something in space that doesn't add up. In the 1800s, astronomers noticed Uranus wasn't staying on its predicted path, and the culprit turned out to be Neptune. Percival Lowell thought Uranus was still misbehaving and went looking for a "Planet X," a search that led to Pluto in 1930. But Pluto proved far too small to explain the trouble. Today, clues come from farther out, in a growing collection of frozen worlds beyond Neptune that move in ways the known planets can't explain. To many astronomers, that hints that something is still out there maybe one planet, maybe more. title: GLP-1 drugs could have a surprisingly large environmental payoff
src: Roslyn Henry and Peter Alexander, The Conversation
author: Roslyn Henry and Peter Alexander, The Conversation
body: GLP-1 weight-loss medicines such as Ozempic and Wegovy could affect much more than the waistlines of the people who take them. If widely used, our new research suggests these appetite-suppressing medicines could transform the global food system and free up vast areas of agricultural land. The global food system is ultimately driven by demand. If people eat less, producers respond, affecting production, prices, trade, and how much land is needed. We used a powerful computer simulation to explore scenarios ranging from GLP-1 use concentrated in high-income countries to widespread global access. With widespread use of these medicines among adults living with obesity, we estimate that reduced calorie intake could prevent up to 6.6 million deaths each year by 2050, while freeing up as much as 32 million hectares of agricultural land—an area slightly larger than Italy—for other uses. title: Moon phase today: What the Moon will look like on November 22, 2026
body: The Full Moon is just around the corner, and tonight the Moon is looking almost completely illuminated. We're still in the Waxing Gibbous phase for now, but it won't be long before visibility hits 100%. What is today's Moon phase? As of Sunday, Nov. 22, the NASA's Daily Moon Guide tracker tells us the Moon is in the Waxing Gibbous phase, with 92% of its surface visible. If you don't have any visual aids, you can still see the Mares Vaporum and Serenitatis, as well as the Aristarchus Plateau. With binoculars, you'll also see the Apennine Mountains, the Gassendi Crater, and the Mare Nectaris. And if you have a telescope, you'll get to see all this plus the Apollo 14 and 17 landing spots, and the Rima Ariadaeus. When is the next Full Moon? The next Full Moon will take place on November 24. What are Moon phases? According to NASA , the Moon goes through a complete cycle of phases roughly every 29.5 days. As it orbits Earth, the portion of its sunlit surface visible to us changes, giving rise to the different lunar phases. The cycle begins with a New Moon, progresses to a Full Moon, and then gradually returns to a New Moon before starting all over again. The eight phases are: New Moon - The Moon is between Earth and the sun, so the side we see is dark (in other words, it's invisible to the eye). Waxing Crescent - A small sliver of light appears on the right side (Northern Hemisphere). First Quarter - Half of the Moon is lit on the right side. It looks like a half-Moon. Waxing Gibbous - More than half is lit up, but it's not quite full yet. Full Moon - The whole face of the Moon

title: Review: Godzilla Minus Zero joins the list of truly stellar sequels
author: Jennifer Ouellette
body: It's a rare thing for a film sequel to match or even surpass its predecessor; The Godfather Part II and Terminator 2: Judgement Day are the best known examples on a pretty short list. Go ahead and add Godzilla Minus Zero to that list. Director Takashi Yamazaki's sequel to his critically acclaimed Godzilla Minus One (2023) is everything one could want in a Godzilla movie: human pathos, great special effects, and, ultimately, two giant kaiju duking it out over who gets to destroy Japan (and eventually the world) the most. (Spoilers for the first film below. Spoilers for Minus Zero but no major reveals until after the gallery. We'll give you a heads-up when we get there.) As I wrote previously , Yamazaki wanted to return to Godzilla’s filmic roots with Minus One , setting the events in postwar Japan and tapping into the monster’s symbolic representation of the Japanese perspective on the 1940s nuclear holocaust—while also incorporating all-too-human themes of guilt and redemption. That first film focused on kamikaze pilot Kōichi Shikishima (Ryunosuke Kamiki), who struggled with survivor’s guilt after he failed to take action when Godzilla attacked the Japanese base on Odo Island in 1945. body: On YouTube , a channel can lose its ad revenue and still have an audience. Its videos can show up in subscribers' feeds, get passed around in group chats, and reach people who've never watched the channel before. That's what happened with Russell Brand 's YouTube channel, which has more than 6 million subscribers. After allegations of rape and sexual assault became public in September 2023, YouTube suspended the channel from its Partner Program , citing a violation of its creator responsibility policy. Brand continued to post commentary on current events and host Christian-themed "Sunday Service" videos with his wife, Laura Gallacher. This month, on Nov. 15, six days after Brand was sentenced to 10 years and six months in prison for rape and sexual assault, Gallacher posted a video to his channel titled "The Good Work Continues" in which she read a message from him denying he had committed the crimes. The hour-long video drew more than 1 million views and prompted a takedown request from the Prison Service of England and Wales , which said the video could cause distress to Brand's victims. body: Just how happy is Rockstar Games with the sales performance of its long-awaited Grand Theft Auto VI ? Here's a clue: it didn't even wait 48 hours before releasing the first-day sales figures. According to its official statement , GTA VI 's "day one retail sales reached $3.79 billion, setting a new record for entertainment across any medium, and becoming the biggest entertainment launch in history." Included in that tally is revenue from an astonishing 32.5 million preorders, making it the most pre-ordered game in history on both Xbox and PlayStation, according to Microsoft, makers of the Xbox game console and Sony, makers of the Playstation, the only two systems that can currently play the game. But it's when you put those numbers into perspective that you get a sense of how astonishingly successful Rockstar's launch truly was. Spider-Man: Brand New Day is the highest-grossing movie of 2026, according to Box Office Mojo , with worldwide ticket sales exceeding $2.5 billion. That film was released at the end of July, more than three months ago, but Grand Theft Auto VI has already exceeded its worldwide box office total by more than a billion dollars. But what if we widened our search? On Box Office Mojo's ranking of the highest-grossing movies of all time , 2019's Avengers: Endgame ranks near the top with worldwide ticket sales of over $2.9 billion still well short of Rockstar's GTA VI score. title: Can Anthropic afford to put safety first?
body: Today, I’m talking with Hayden Field, The Verge ’s senior AI reporter, about the Anthropic IPO for the third and final episode in our series about AI in real life. The AI lab behind Claude went public on the Nasdaq last Thursday. The numbers are gigantic, but not really that important for this conversation, except to say that Anthropic has become one of the most valuable companies on the planet. The real story is what happens now — and whether Anthropic can continue to thread the needle of caring about and investing in AI safety while also being a public company beholden to shareholders. Oh, and it also continuously growing the amount of money it makes so it can keep paying its ever-increasing compute bills, which total roughly $900 billion over the coming years. All of these ideas sit in a fascinating tension with one another, and so Hayden and I really tried to break down how we think this might play out as Anthropic navigates the pressures of the public markets. You’ll hear us talk about the company’s unique corporate governance structure , something that is especially relevant in the wake of the ongoing Jensen Huang saga. We also get into why OpenAI seems happy to have let Anthropic go public first , and why Anthropic’s whole pitch to big customers boils down to the same safety branding that now sits in conflict with the profit-oriented part of its business. Before we get going, do me a favor and subscribe to Decoder on YouTube, where we put out new episodes every Monday and Thursday. title: “Race realism” isn’t realistic—and it isn’t good science
src: Jonathan R. Goodman and Rebecca Sear, The Conversation
author: Jonathan R. Goodman and Rebecca Sear, The Conversation
body: At this year’s World Economic Forum meeting in Davos, US President Donald Trump stated that people from Somalia have low IQs. “I always say these are low-IQ people,” he said in his speech. His son, Donald Trump Jr, made a similar statement about Haitian people in 2024 (Trump’s government has since ended the protected status of both Somali and Haitian migrants in the US). These statements and their consequences are symptoms of a growing trend in Western politics: the re-emergence of racial views of human nature that have been largely in hiding for the past 70 years. Narratives about the innate intellectual inferiority of black or brown people compared with white people—which can still be found in academic journals today—are fuelling far-right propaganda in some of the world’s largest democracies. Such claims underpin misinformation strategies on social media and bolster political movements. These narratives are sometimes euphemistically referred to as “ race science ” or more recently “race realism.” But, as we argue, they are not actually scientific. One member of this community, Nathan Cofnas , recently attracted public attention by accusing the late Jason Arday of plagiarism. Read full article Comments

title: The Boox Picco made me love tiny e-readers
body: I don't get the hype of tiny e-readers. I've used a ton of e-readers Kindles , Kobos, and Boox and I thought they were just the right size, and I wasn't craving a smaller e-reader. But plenty of people clearly are, as I've spent hours browsing Reddit and reading about how people use their tiny e-readers. Boox is one of the first big brands to launch a mini e-reader of its own, the Picco. Other Boox e-readers run on Android, but the Picco does not. I expected to be underwhelmed, but I'm glad to be wrong. The Boox Picco has given me a whole new love for tiny e-readers, and I finally understand their appeal. Credit: Samantha Mangino / Mashable The physical design of the Boox Picco isn't all that different from other tiny e-readers, but what matters is literally what's on the inside. The user interface is exceptionally easy to navigate and straightforward it's pretty pared back compared to Kindle or Kobo. The Picco combines physical buttons and touchscreen controls. The 'bookshelf' section is the device's native library. 'Transfer' lets you move books from the Boox Tile app on your phone to the device; 'Apps' offers a limited selection of pre-downloaded apps; and 'Settings' is exactly as it says. title: Voyager 1 had a data outage when it hit one light day. It still does.
body: While Voyager 1 pushed past the one light-day distance milestone, the 49-year-old probe actually hadn't sent any science or engineering information home for days. The trouble started Nov. 14 , and it hasn't let up. Voyager 1 still beams a steady radio signal to Earth, which tells engineers the spacecraft is alive and its antenna still points at Earth. But the signal carries no information about the probe's health or what its instruments are measuring, and engineers don't yet know why. Voyager 1 crossed the milestone at 5:16 a.m. ET Nov. 18, about 16.1 billion miles away, according to NASA . No other human-made object has traveled so far. Because the probe's radio signal takes a full day to cross space , the team didn't get word until 5:16 a.m. ET Nov. 19, when a ground antenna near Madrid picked it up. NASA marked the achievement Thursday with an hourlong celebration at its Jet Propulsion Laboratory in Southern California that may have overshadowed the problem. Panelists shared memories of the mission, the agency played a video from fans around the world, and astronaut Jessica Watkins aboard the International Space Station provided a recorded tribute. The host covered the data outage in two sentences before opening the floor to questions. Officials delved into the spacecraft's current condition only after a reporter asked how the spacecraft was doing. "We have an anomaly that is not something unseen before," said Suzanne Dodd, Voyager's project manager. "We do have a very strong carrier signal. title: Thank the gods, Percy Jackson remembered it should be funny
body: Disney+'s Percy Jackson and the Olympians series has done an admirable job of adapting the Greek mythology-inspired adventures of Rick Riordan's novels . But it has consistently struggled with a key aspect of of the books: their humor. The book series are narrated by Percy Jackson (Walker Scobell) himself, whose internal monologue contains its fair range of sass and hilariously deadpan descriptions of the strange things that happen to him. Case in point, every book's irreverent chapter titles, which kick off with the iconic "I Accidentally Vaporize My Pre-Algebra Teacher" and go on to include such hits as "I Battle My Jerk Relative" and "Everybody Hates Me but the Horse." The TV series borrows these chapter headings for its own episode titles, but loses a significant chunk of the humor that make them land on the page. It sands down much of the wisecracking banter between Percy and his questing companions, turning them into more stoic fantasy heroes. Yes, Season 2 features one of the books' funniest moments: the fan-favorite scene of Grover (Aryan Simhadri) wearing a wedding dress to escape from cyclops Polyphemus. (It throws Percy in a dress too for good measure.) But it also misses out on the smaller wordplay or misunderstandings that drew big laughs from the books, like when Percy mistakes the word "hubris" for "hummus." It's a solid joke, as well as a reminder that Percy is just a kid caught in the crossfires of a mythic war. author: Jon Brodkin
body: The Federal Communications Commission ordered California to stop enforcing its Carrier of Last Resort (COLR) rules against AT T, setting up another battle between the Trump administration and California over the state's right to enforce its own telecom laws and regulations. AT T's status as a Carrier of Last Resort in California requires it to offer telephone service to any potential customer in its territory. AT T wants to stop offering basic phone service to new customers and discontinue service for 184,000 residential customers and 15,000 business customers on June 1, 2027. The order released today granted AT T's request to preempt state rules, following up on the FCC's previous approval of AT T's petition to discontinue service. title: Google rolls out new search homepage with AI chat history and no search button
author: Ryan Whitwam
body: Google's flagship search experience is evolving into an AI experience with stunning speed. Even time-tested elements of search are getting AI makeovers, and the latest to get this treatment is the search homepage on Google.com. A redesign that's been in testing for the last few weeks is now official, bringing easier access to AI chats and dropping the dedicated search button entirely. Google search VP Robby Stein confirmed on X that Google is deploying the new desktop search page after a successful test. The page will now have a few more buttons under the search bar, all connected to AI features. There's an image generation button, one for analyzing files, and one for brainstorming with Gemini. The "I'm Feeling Lucky" button remains, but the Google Search button that used to sit next to it is gone. The search button has obviously been a part of Google's search page forever. However, it wasn't in a very convenient location in the modern interface. When you begin typing a query, the autocomplete suggestions cover that button. You have to click out of the text field to access the button, which is an extra step compared to simply mashing the Enter key to run your search. Read full article Comments

title: Meta reconsiders 2030 net-zero goal amid record emissions from AI data centers
author: Jeremy Hsu
body: Meta’s executives are rethinking the company’s original goal of achieving net-zero emissions by 2030. That revelation in Meta’s latest sustainability report comes as the company reported a record percentage increase in greenhouse gas emissions that exceeds any other Big Tech competitor racing to build new AI data centers. The company’s 2026 sustainability report claims that “our long-term ambitions haven’t changed, but our operating environment has,” according to an introduction from Rachel Peterson, vice president of data centers at Meta, and Blair Swedeen, global head of net zero and sustainability at Meta. In the November 19, 2026, report, they attributed the changing conditions and the need for a rethink to how “demand for AI infrastructure has grown faster than almost anyone projected.” “We are re-evaluating our timelines, sequencing, and interim milestones—including the 2030 timeframe for our net zero emissions goal and our near-term intensity targets—so our approach reflects current operating realities while keeping progress transparent year over year,” Peterson and Swedeen wrote in the report.
